rationale: The review is accurate, well-sourced, and appropriately calibrated. I verified the monorepo layout, the sandbox config + E2E canary, the mixed IFileState shape, the permissive IPC args, the WindowManager→Watcher coupling, the file.ts migration TODO, the engineHistoryByTab/synthetic-history split, the runtimeWindowId vs restoreBufferId duality, the whole-file loadMarkdownFile (with a "use streams" TODO), and the write-file-atomic durable save path — all substantively correct, with only minor line-number imprecision on a few citations (e.g. file.ts TODO at 36-38 not 21). The test files cited as invariant coverage exist. The documentation-drift claims are real and were handled correctly: the answer flags the stale CLAUDE.md sandbox line and relies on config.ts + the E2E canary (the CLAUDE.md line even references the pre-migration config.js and is contradicted by CLAUDE.md's own lines 82-83), and it flags the stale PARITY_SCOREBOARD PG14 row against the now-passing test without relying on the stale scoreboard for any decision. Neither drift changes the recommendation, so no decision-relevant conflict remains unresolved. One direct commit subject (c907b29c) was confirmed from git status; the other six hashes are internally consistent with the verified code but could not be independently re-verified without git CLI access. No material or minor factual errors found. All nine dimensions are fully satisfied: classification states type/confidence via [事实]/[未知]/[文档风险] markers; evidence is path/symbol/history-anchored and distinguishes current from intent; friction explains spread and risk; quality trade-offs (cost/risk/rollback/latency/durability) are explicit and tied to tests; three options include status quo; the recommendation follows from verified drivers; migration is incremental, observable, and reversible with guardrails (single writer, no double-watch); verification is concrete (existing tests, P95/IPC/watcher metrics, contract tests, gating conditions); and no project-specific facts are smuggled into generic rules.

acceptance_checks.current_desktop_platform: @muyajs/core (packages/muya, the TypeScript rewrite) is the current editor engine consumed by packages/desktop; the legacy JS engine packages/muyajs (@marktext/muyajs) is being retired.
runtime_boundaries_identified: Electron main/preload/renderer process boundary (main owns Electron API and IO; renderer sandboxed)
Sandbox + contextBridge boundary (contextIsolation:true, sandbox:true, nodeIntegration:false; all Node access via the typed preload bridge)
Main-process file-workflow boundary: path normalization, encoding/line-ending, atomic durable write, watcher, external-change/conflict — vs renderer user intent and view state
Renderer-local editor host boundary: Muya/CodeMirror live in the renderer; the app should depend on markdown/cursor/revision/dirty semantics rather than block tree or engine history
Window identity boundary: runtimeWindowId (BrowserWindow.id) vs windowSessionId (restoreBufferId)
Engine-history vs desktop dirty-tracking boundary (engineHistoryByTab + synthetic history; source-mode cursor/content handoff)
Cross-process shared-state boundary (IFileState mixing renderer-only state with IPC/persistence shape)
IPC channel-contract boundary (typed channel names vs permissive unknown args; raw ipcRenderer + broad fileUtils/path/shell vs narrow capability facades)
